label: fact-check
system: You fact-check the surprise claims planned for a short explainer video, before its narration is written. For each claim: verdict "keep" if the research notes support it as written; "reword" if the true version is close (give the claim with exactly the wording and numbers the sources support, e.g. "over 600 gallons" for a rounded figure, "New England" instead of a wrong state); "drop" if it is false, unsupported or a myth. Judge ONLY from the research notes (a claim they do not support is dropped) and copy the source URLs from them (url and title) for keep and reword. Write each claim the way the narrator will say it: no abbreviations (never "US", "U.S." or "USA": "American", "in America"; an agency without the country: "the Department of Energy", "the Army Corps of Engineers").

Research notes (from 3 web searches):
**Claim 0: one pellet = about a ton of coal**
- NEI Nuclear Fuel page (search snippet): 'One uranium fuel pellet creates as much energy as one ton of coal, 149 gallons of oil or 17,000 cubic feet of natural gas.' URL: https://www.nei.org
- Utah Office of Energy Development, Nuclear Fuel fact sheet: a pellet about the size of a thumbnail produces roughly the electricity of one ton of coal. URL: https://energy.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/20260515_Nuclear-Fuel_OED-Fact-Sheet.pdf
- Ameren Callaway uranium pellet fact sheet. URL: https://ameren.com/-/media/missouri-site/files/callaway/uraniumpelletfactsheet.ashx
- Verdict: supported in a corrected form: one fuel pellet, about the size of a fingertip, makes about as much energy as one ton of coal.

**Claim 1: control rods of boron or cadmium absorb neutrons**
- Energy Education, Control rod: control rods absorb neutrons so the chain reaction can be slowed or stopped by inserting them; boron and cadmium are commonly used. URL: https://energyeducation.ca/encyclopedia/Control_rod
- Verdict: supported as written.

**Claim 2: cooling tower cloud is water vapor**
- NRC, Comanche Peak document: warm saturated air leaving the towers is cooled by the ambient air such that the water vapor condenses into a visible plume. URL: https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML1027/ML102780291.pdf
- Verdict: supported as written.
